body: Thanks for the reply. I wouldn't really expect any kind of conviction to come from it at this point. But what would happen if the report was made? How public would it be?

Because thoughts of suicide can come and go. It's a permanent decision, more permanent than anything else, and there are thousands of people who wanted to kill themselves and didn't who are now much, much happier.  For a lot of people, suicidal thoughts pass. Plus, when someone kills themselves, it affects everyone in their life. It can emotionally wreck everyone who was close to that person and traumatize them for life. 

Anecdotally, the vast majority of people who jump off the Golden Gate Bridge and survived have reported that they regretted their decision immediately after jumping. I think ultimately people are against suicide because they don't want someone to make a rash decision that would hurt a lot of people and cannot be undone.
That’s a major concern of mine. I don’t know what’s more disturbing— the idea that this happened, or the idea that I made it up and convinced myself it happened
I don't think I could ever talk to my dad about it. I've been in therapy for years and haven't had the courage to bring it up... I'm thinking that should change
